messages.author: 9ee7ccab51acb1f5
messages.subject: subset.capthist
parts:
Hello secr masters,


I am working on roe deer density estimation. The sampling design was 29 camera-traps/km2 during 153 days of sampling. I would like to sub-sample the data to know how density results change with reduced number of cameras and reduced number of days. This will allow me to optimise the sampling effort for future studies and also to assess the appropriate sampling effort to identify a big proportion of the standing male roe deer population.


In my opinion, the best option would be to use the function subset.capthist(), subsetting for decreasing occasions and traps. Ideally, using a bootstrap approach with 100 iterations and plot the density results for the camera-subsampling and temporal-subsampling. Do you think that this make sense? Do you have other suggestions?


Thank you very much for your attention.

Best regards,

Amael Hinojo.

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: subset.capthist
parts:
You could do that. I wouldn't take the results too seriously as an indication of what might happen next time you sample, so 100 bootstraps might be over the top - maybe 1 would be enough to give you the picture.

You could also plug your parameter estimates into secrdesignapp (https://www.stats.otago.ac.nz/secrdesignapp/). That scrolls to a maximum of 100 occasions in the current version, but you can type in 153 or whatever. Subsetting detector locations is a bit trickier in secrdesignapp, but you can generate random or regular configurations in a region.

Murray
